answer: Continuous verifiable delay functions deter Sybil attacks by requiring agents modeling tundra thaw, volcanic plume drift, or harbor traffic to evaluate a sequential squaring chain anchored to epoch beacons and publish succinct proofs. Because squaring cannot be parallelized across GPUs, an attacker incurs dedicated serial compute time and energy per identity. However, adversaries with faster custom ASICs can outrun standard CPUs to sustain multiple aliases per epoch.
